content.text: A useful elementary battery model tracks stored energy in kWh, charge input and delivered discharge power. This says nothing about Coulombic efficiency, calendar aging, nonlinear voltage, cell mismatch or safe charge acceptance. A physically accountable model rejects a step that exceeds capacity rather than silently clipping storage and hiding the excess energy.

content.text: Electricity can be stored indirectly as gravitational potential, kinetic energy, compressed fluid, phase-change heat or chemical energy. Each mechanism has a different energy density, response time, efficiency, site requirement and durability. Pumped hydro returns water downhill after using electricity to pump it upward, with a round-trip loss. Flywheel energy grows with the square of angular speed, but mechanical stress and containment impose limits. Sensible thermal storage uses heat capacity; phase-change storage adds latent heat at appropriate temperatures. Compressed-air storage interacts with thermodynamics of compression and expansion, so a pressure-only calculation is inadequate. Selecting a technology requires a service definition: seconds of fast response, days of shifting, industrial process heat or seasonal energy supply.

title: Water heating, thermal energy and disinfection boundaries — service principle

applicability: Offline survival-energy science and reconstruction teaching under stipulated model inputs
assumptions: Declared SI units, positive/negative sign convention and model boundary required
limitations: Any claim of real shelter adequacy requires safe indoor temperature and ventilation assessment, not just energy balance. A structure can have low modeled heat loss but dangerous combustion or CO hazards.
content.text: In prolonged power outages, reducing thermal losses can improve survivability without adding generation. A simple quasi-steady building model uses aggregate heat-loss coefficient UA, in watts per kelvin, and sums positive indoor–outdoor temperature degree-hours. It gives an approximate thermal-energy requirement but not a prescription for heating equipment. Infiltration, wind, solar gains, internal moisture, occupancy, thermal mass, ventilation and freeze risks can dominate real performance. A building may become unsafe before a calculated energy budget is exhausted. The model must clearly separate desired indoor temperatures, expected weather and heating system conversion efficiency, all of which require evidence and qualified assessment.

title: Thermal shelter, insulation and degree-hours — service principle

applicability: Offline survival-energy science and reconstruction teaching under stipulated model inputs
assumptions: Declared SI units, positive/negative sign convention and model boundary required
limitations: Heat pumps are not perpetual motion machines, and high COP is not necessarily high energy availability during an outage. The source heat reservoir, inverter peak power and controls must be present.
content.text: Electric resistance heaters convert electrical work into local heat approximately at a one-for-one energy ratio at the point of use. Heat pumps use external work to move heat from a colder source to a warmer sink, so the delivered thermal energy can exceed the input electrical energy. The coefficient of performance (COP) is therefore not a conventional power-conversion efficiency and may exceed one without violating energy conservation. Ideal reversible COP depends on absolute temperature difference, while actual performance depends on design, source conditions, defrost cycles, load, humidity, refrigerant and auxiliary heat. A nominal COP label at one rating condition is not a verified cold-weather field value.

limitations: Never infer a safe operating duration from fuel volume alone; startup, transient loading, engine condition and hazardous emissions are missing. Improper utility backfeeding can injure others even when local voltage appears acceptable.
content.text: Fuel-powered generation can provide energy during renewable shortages, but it introduces combustion gases, fire, noise, fuel quality, maintenance and electrical backfeed hazards. The first calculation relates fuel volume to chemical energy and assumed electrical conversion efficiency. That arithmetic cannot tell whether a generator is safely installed, properly isolated from the utility, ventilated, maintained or able to provide stable AC power under real load. CDC guidance warns that carbon monoxide from portable generators can cause fatal poisoning in enclosed or nearby spaces. A research reference should preserve these safety boundaries as part of the physics, not present an incomplete fuel-to-kWh calculation as a practical operating procedure.

title: Fuel-backed generation: conservation, carbon monoxide and backfeed — service principle

applicability: Offline survival-energy science and reconstruction teaching under stipulated model inputs
assumptions: Declared SI units, positive/negative sign convention and model boundary required
limitations: Do not label maximum unserved energy among a few cases as a universal worst case. Real protection, failure modes, load volatility and supply variance are absent from energy-only models.
content.text: A survival power service is judged by the services it reliably provides. In an offline energy ledger, unserved energy is the positive sum of demanded electrical energy not supplied during the given intervals; the proportion unserved is that amount divided by requested energy. Counting the number of intervals with a shortage is another descriptive statistic. In probabilistic reliability analysis, expected energy not served (EENS) requires a probability measure over system states, weather, outages and failures; loss-of-load expectation and probability similarly depend on an event model. A fixed synthetic scenario does not establish an expectation. Explicitly naming denominators and observed or stipulated inputs prevents inflated claims of system endurance.

content.text: If energy science must survive the loss of internet access and specialized vendors, numerical results need more than a copied constant. Each measurable quantity requires a definition, unit, reference state, measuring instrument, calibration method, uncertainties, and original evidence where permitted. The NIST 2022 CODATA adjustment supplies recommended values as of its declared scientific edition; exact SI defining constants must be distinguished from experimentally adjusted constants with standard uncertainties. The current Atlas contains derived constants in its own JSON but does not retain the original NIST publication bytes. This remains a documented preservation deficit, not a reason to invent a primary-source file or label a table authenticated from memory.

applicability: Offline survival-energy science and reconstruction teaching under stipulated model inputs
assumptions: Declared SI units, positive/negative sign convention and model boundary required
limitations: This chapter is an offline educational reconstruction, not a construction guide for high-voltage wiring, improvised fuel, unsafe heating or potentially contaminated water. The full body of human energy science extends far beyond 50 chapters.
content.text: A future reader with only text and a calculator should be able to reconstruct a minimal energy budget: identify services, measure or reasonably estimate demand, convert all quantities to SI units, document sources and assumptions, calculate resource output and conversion limits, track storage and losses, and compare scenario shortfalls. The reader must also understand where a model stops: independently safe wiring, generator placement, battery fire protection, potable water treatment, fuel logistics and utility interconnection require contemporary local expertise and tested equipment. The Atlas should preserve those boundaries, not hand-wave them away with a high test count. Its most important survival property is to retain methods for discovering what is unknown and rebuilding evidence when equipment or primary publications are missing.
